provocation: Every idea here assumes the authored content is the thing that drifts and the vendor is stable. `.drift-state.json` says the opposite: five findings are `cli-behind` and `marketplace-behind`, one is `copy-drifted`. So the moment `claude` or `codex` renames a settings key, deprecates `skillOverrides`, or changes where skills are discovered, a materializer that pins content stops being a repair tool and becomes a downgrade tool that faithfully restores a schema the CLI no longer reads — and it will report success. Who owns that migration, the plugin or the vendor? And a sharper version: the 1-shared-line-in-60 diff proves cross-harness parity is not achievable, because Codex has no mechanism for `skillOverrides` at all and the AGENTS.md says so in prose. What if the shipped artifact is a capability map — for each of the ~60 assertions, which harness can actually enforce it, which can only be told about it in prose, and which will silently ignore it — and materialization is just that map filtered by the local harness's version? Then a vendor upgrade that adds an enforcement mechanism turns a prose rule into a real setting, and the "one command" is the only thing that would ever notice.

top3.text: The public package ships only holes (topology, fence markers, schema, ownership rules) with content pulled from a user-pointed source, plus a release gate failing if any private byte appears in the tarball.

deepened.idea: A content-free materializer on chezmoi's model — public binary, private source checkout, per-entry state — but with harness-aware hole kinds (JSON-pointer subtree, fence-delimited region, dir-symlink-into-source, lockfile install-set, marketplace install-set) so the unit of idempotency is the hole rather than the file, which is what lets drift repair be surgical on files the harness itself writes to.
deepened.sketch: The public package ships `topology.json` and zero content: an ordered list of holes, each with an address (a path, a path plus JSON pointer, a path plus fence-marker name, or a symlink path plus target expression), a kind, and an owner (package / source / harness / user); `npx harness materialize <source>` clones the user-pointed source to a fixed path and reads values keyed by those same addresses, so no value ever lives in the package. Because the source checkout is persistent rather than a transient fetch, directory holes materialize as symlinks into it — authored skills stay live-editable, `git status` there stays the honest answer — while single files are copied, since an editor's write-temp-and-rename silently replaces a file symlink with a regular file. Fence markers carry the markdown and TOML holes (`CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `config.toml`), but `settings.json` has no comment syntax, so it is JSON-pointer holes plus a sidecar ownership map — and it is the file that most needs one, because the harness writes into it at runtime. Each hole is repaired by three-way merge: base is a per-hole receipt of what the tool last wrote (`~/.claude/.harness-receipt.json`), ours is live bytes, theirs is source bytes; identical is a no-op, live-equals-base writes, all-three-differ surfaces a conflict and never clobbers, and on a fresh machine with no receipt the owner column decides and a receipt is created. Skills and plugins are declarative install-set holes: the lockfile's content hashes and `extraKnownMarketplaces`/`enabledPlugins` are inputs to `npx skills add -g` and the plugin installer, with convergence defined as "hash already on disk", so a re-run installs nothing. The implementation is a plain CLI runnable with neither harness installed, which both solves the chicken-and-egg (a plugin cannot materialize `enabledPlugins` if it must first be an enabled plugin) and makes "works on both" cost only two thin skill wrappers over one binary. Release safety is class-level rather than a literal denylist — a committed list of your own private strings is itself the leak — so the gate rejects any absolute home-style path, bare email, or `github.com/<owner>` outside the package org anywhere in the built tarball, and positively requires that materializing the shipped fixture source into a scratch `$HOME` reproduces the fixture's expected tree. The prompt-driven wizard survives as an optional front end that renders the per-hole diff and takes the accept-in-one-word, but it is no longer the mechanism, so an unattended re-run is possible.
deepened.loadBearingRisk: The receipt is the merge base, and it is the only thing separating "repair" from "clobber". Fresh-machine absence is designed for (owner decides, receipt written), so the residual risk is receipt loss or multi-machine staleness: I change `model` from `sonnet` to `opus` on the laptop and never run capture; the desktop's receipt still records `sonnet`, so on the laptop the next repair sees live != base with theirs == base and reverts my deliberate edit as drift, silently and with the same code path that legitimately repairs. Every dotfile manager that skipped per-entry state degraded to two-way comparison and had to choose between clobbering local edits and never converging. If the receipt cannot be made durable and per-machine-honest, the settled "safely re-runnable drift repair" constraint fails and this becomes a one-shot installer with extra ceremony.
deepened.firstStep: Write `bin/harness-extract.py`, which walks the live `~/.claude`, `~/.codex`, and `~/.agents` and emits three artifacts: `topology.json` (addresses, kinds, owners — no values), a `values/` tree destined for the private source, and an ownership classification for every `settings.json` JSON pointer. Prove the split by materializing into a scratch `$HOME` and diffing — `diff -r` for trees, `jq -S` for JSON — which validates that the hole vocabulary is complete before any packaging or content work exists. Seed the ownership column with evidence already in hand: `diff <(jq -S . ~/.claude/settings.json) <(jq -S . ~/harness-backup/claude/settings.json)` returns exactly one key, `agentPushNotifEnabled`, a harness-written runtime toggle rather than an authored value — the first entry in the harness-owned set, and the concrete proof that whole-file copying is the wrong unit.
childIdeas: `harness capture`, the inverse traversal: read live bytes at every hole address and write them back into the source checkout. This eliminates the copy-drift class that the README's manual `cp ... && git status` block exists to paper over — and that `.drift-state.json` currently reports against `claude/settings.json` — and it is what keeps the receipt honest on the machine you actually work on, which is the direct mitigation for the load-bearing risk. Per the repo's own ordering, eliminating the drift beats detecting it.

Fixture-as-seed: the `fixtures/example-source/` that exists for the round-trip release gate doubles as the documented source-repo format and as the seed a user with no source yet materializes from. One artifact serves test, documentation, and onboarding, and the private repo never has to be shown in order to explain what a source looks like.

Unify the drift vocabulary: make `harness-drift-check.py`'s finding kinds (`copy-drifted`, `marketplace-behind`, `cli-behind`) be hole kinds addressed the same way, so a drift report is literally an executable repair plan — `harness repair --only copy-drifted`. Detection stays a separate concern, as settled, but the two halves share one address space instead of two hand-synced inventories of what exists.

Layered sources plus an explicit target home: accept N sources merged in address order (org baseline, then team, then personal overlay, last writer wins per hole), which turns the same public package into team onboarding while keeping each layer's privacy independent. Because materialize already parameterizes the destination, `--home /tmp/scratch` then builds a disposable profile — for reproducing an agent bug without your real config, bisecting which harness setting changed a behavior, or provisioning a devcontainer or cloud sandbox with a byte-identical harness.

Schema lint as a scheduled test: derive the expected `settings.json` pointer set from `json.schemastore.org/claude-code-settings.json` (already referenced by the live file) and fail a nightly job when either vendor adds, renames, or removes a key the topology claims to own. This converts silent ownership-manifest staleness into a dated test failure — the same move as the README's Codex description-truncation finding, which turned an invisible degradation into a measured one.

deepened.idea: Materialize assertions, not files: ~60 independently owned facts, each applied and repaired alone, with settings.json a render nobody owns end to end.
deepened.sketch: The unit is an assertion — (address, desired value, policy) — where an address is a JSON pointer into ~/.claude/settings.json, a key path in ~/.codex/config.toml, a marker-delimited block inside CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md, a symlink path, or a probe-and-install command for a marketplace plugin or a locked skill. Roughly 60 authored assertions instantiate into several hundred applied ones: the symlink topology is two rules expanded over ~/.agents/.skill-lock.json (26 links under ~/.claude/skills, 26 more under ~/.codex/skills), not 52 hand-written facts. Apply sets one address; verify reads that same address back; nothing ever copies a whole file, so keys the plugin ships no assertion for — theme, model, effortLevel, advisorModel — survive byte-identical, which is the whole point given that Claude Code writes no default settings.json to diff against. Each assertion carries a reconciliation policy: enforce (skillOverrides.grilling = name-only, the symlinks), enforce-superset (extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins — add mine, never remove yours), or seed-once (write if absent, then the user owns it). Every write records the value it wrote into ~/.claude/harness-state.json, which supplies the merge base for the next run: current == last-written means drift, repair it silently; current != last-written means the human changed their mind, report and offer to adopt, never revert. The two prose files are one template with a `harness` variable rendered into both targets, so the Codex description-truncation rule is a variable rather than a fork, and when markers are absent the block is appended under a fixed heading — that first-insertion rule is what makes replace-between-markers idempotent from run two onward. Cross-harness support falls out because the engine is a program the plugin ships (`bin/harness-apply --plan|--apply`), not a prompt: Claude Code invokes it from a slash command, Codex from a skill that runs the same binary, with the usual sandbox approval escalation for writes into ~/.claude/. The pre-apply read is convergence plumbing, not drift detection — the weekly cron keeps that job.
deepened.loadBearingRisk: An assertion cannot, on its own, tell "this drifted, repair it" from "the human deliberately changed it, adopt it" — both look like current != desired. The only thing that separates them is the recorded last-applied value, so the state file is load-bearing and it is exactly the artifact most likely to be missing, stale, or wiped. The sharp edge is the fresh machine that is not actually fresh: no state file plus an existing hand-tuned settings.json means every seed-once assertion looks like drift, and a confident first run vandalizes the config it was invoked to protect. The rule that closes it is "no merge base → treat every existing value as intent, apply only structural assertions (symlinks, installs, absent-marker blocks)". The failure asymmetry is favorable and worth designing toward: a write that lands but fails to record its state degrades to under-repair, which is safe; only revert-without-base destroys work.
deepened.firstStep: Implement the JSON-pointer assertion kind end to end — apply, verify, state-record — for exactly three enforce-policy keys in the live ~/.claude/settings.json: skillOverrides.grilling, one enabledPlugins entry, and one extraKnownMarketplaces entry. Then prove the two things that decide whether the whole design stands: that the ~40 unowned keys round-trip byte-identical through a write, and that a Claude Code session exiting after your write does not clobber it (the read-modify-write race against the harness's own rewrite-on-exit). Three assertions is enough to falsify the approach; the inventory of the other 57 is worthless if the round-trip loses a key.
childIdeas: The wizard survives as the resolver, not the installer: it is invoked only for assertions whose value is marked from-user and is currently unresolved, so first run asks about six things and every subsequent drift repair asks zero — the human-in-the-loop step shrinks from 'review every file' to 'answer what nobody could know'.

Assertion contribution as a plugin protocol: any installed plugin ships assertions against the shared settings.json, so extraKnownMarketplaces and enabledPlugins become a computed union across plugins instead of one author's snapshot, and uninstall becomes 'retract my assertions' rather than a hand-edit that leaves orphaned marketplace entries behind.

Adopt mode: promote a recorded divergence back into the seed (or into the private answer cache), turning the three-way state file from a one-way safety brake into genuine two-way sync — and giving the existing drift-check cron a disposition it currently lacks, namely 'this is now intended, stop reporting it'.

The private repo collapses into a from-user answer cache: CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md and config.toml stop being hand-maintained copies and become renders of (public seed assertions + private answers), which dissolves the copy-then-commit refresh ritual and the copy-drifted finding class entirely rather than continuing to repair them.

Assertion-level CI: because every assertion has an isolated apply/verify pair, the full set is runnable against a throwaway HOME on every commit, so fresh-machine materialization becomes a test rather than an annual gamble — and an upstream schema change (a renamed settings key, a moved skills directory) surfaces as a failing assertion in CI instead of a silent no-op on someone's new laptop.

deepened.idea: Ship the materializer as one dependency-free `harness-apply` script driven by a profile directory that mirrors the target tree plus a small manifest of non-file verbs; the Claude plugin command and the Codex prompt are three-line shims that run `--plan` then `--apply`.
deepened.sketch: Ship one file, `harness-apply` — `/bin/sh`-compatible, no jq and no python, Linux/WSL first (macOS means bash 3.2, so no associative arrays) — alongside a *profile*: a directory that mirrors the target tree (`home/.claude/settings.json`, `home/.codex/config.toml`, `home/.claude/CLAUDE.md`) plus a plain-text `manifest` carrying the verbs a file can't express: `link`, `marketplace`, `plugin`, `skill <source> <name>`. The private repo is just one profile the script is pointed at, and the package ships a seed profile, so private config stays an input and never the package source. Apply order is dependency-shaped — dirs, files, marketplaces/plugins, skills, links — because `skills add -g -a claude-code` creates `~/.claude/skills/<name>` itself and the `~/.codex/skills/<name> -> ~/.claude/skills/<name>` hub links cannot exist until the skill does. Every verb has one shape: read desired, read actual, `ok` if equal, `create` if absent, and on a difference consult a line-oriented ledger (`<sha>\t<path>`, so nothing parses JSON at apply time) — ledger hash matches what we last wrote means upstream drift and gets repaired, ledger hash mismatched means a human edited it, so write `<target>.incoming` and report `conflict` rather than clobber. `.skill-lock.json` is deliberately not a file verb: `skills add` rewrites it on every install, so hashing it would report conflict forever; the manifest carries skill lines generated at capture time, and the skill verb's idempotence test is "`~/.agents/skills/<name>` exists", not re-running the installer, because re-running updates and an update is not a repair. Legs whose tool is missing — node for `skills`, git for marketplaces, the harness binary for plugin installs — report `deferred` instead of failing, so a machine with neither harness still gets every file and a later re-run finishes the rest. `--plan` is the default and prints the table of exactly what `--apply` would write while touching nothing; `--apply` acts; both exit non-zero if any line is a conflict. The Claude command and the Codex prompt are then literally the same three lines: run `--plan`, show the table, run `--apply` on one word from the user.
deepened.loadBearingRisk: The plugin surface may not be file-materializable at all. `settings.json`'s `enabledPlugins` and `extraKnownMarketplaces` are only declarations; the real state lives in harness-owned files this machine already has — `~/.claude/plugins/installed_plugins.json` (absolute `installPath`s, versions, `gitCommitSha`, per-project scopes), `known_marketplaces.json`, and the `marketplaces/` and `cache/` git clones. If Claude Code does not reconcile those from `settings.json` on launch, the script must shell out to `claude plugin install`, which requires the harness the script is built to assume does not exist, and the single command degrades into "run, launch Claude once, run again." Hand-writing `installed_plugins.json` is not an escape: its contents are machine facts (resolved paths, fetched SHAs) the script cannot invent. A second, quieter version of the same risk: if the harness rewrites `settings.json` itself on launch, the ledger's "hash mismatch means a human edited it" inference gains a third case and every run reports a false conflict.
deepened.firstStep: Settle the reconciliation question empirically on a scratch HOME before writing any verb code: `mkdir -p /tmp/h/.claude`, write only a `settings.json` containing one `extraKnownMarketplaces` entry and one matching `enabledPlugins` entry, run `HOME=/tmp/h claude -p "hi"` once non-interactively, then inspect whether `/tmp/h/.claude/plugins/{known_marketplaces.json,installed_plugins.json,marketplaces/,cache/}` materialized. The same run answers the second question for free — `diff` the `settings.json` you wrote against the one left behind to see whether the harness self-edits it, which decides between whole-file hashing and key-level compare with a documented ignore list. The outcome picks the largest branch in the script: `plugin` is a file verb, or a shell-out verb that must be marked `deferred` on a bare machine.
childIdeas: Make the shim a SKILL.md instead of a plugin command: one file installed through the same `skills add` path reaches both harnesses via the existing ~/.codex/skills -> ~/.claude/skills -> ~/.agents/skills topology, so materializing skills materializes the entry point — the tool self-hosts and day-N repair needs no plugin or marketplace at all.

Add `--capture`, the inverse run: walk the same manifest and copy the live tree back into the profile directory, regenerating the skill lines from the lockfile. Backup and restore collapse into one program run in two directions, which retires the hand-run `cp` refresh block and the five hand-maintained copies with it.

Layer profiles: a base profile plus a host overlay applied on top, so WSL-vs-macOS path translation, the statusline command path, and machine-local permissions live in the overlay while the authored content stays single-sourced. Overlay resolution is last-writer-wins per path, which needs no new syntax.

Lean on the exit-code contract as a gate elsewhere: the same `--plan` invocation becomes a container `RUN` line for headless agent images, a CI step that fails when a runner's harness is stale, and a `SessionStart` hook that says one line when the live tree has diverged from the profile.

Publish the ledger as the substrate the separate drift detector consumes: it already records, per path, the exact bytes this tool last wrote, which is precisely the baseline a detector needs to tell upstream movement apart from a deliberate local edit — and it lets the detector's issue body name the repairing command instead of describing the fix in prose.
